messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Automated alert: elevated 5xx rate (svc=embeddings-usw) starting ~10m ago. Paging primary oncall. Logs indicate KV eviction spikes + backend OOMs. Initial spike: ~12% error rate, some 503s to a subset of tenant keys. Link: https://sentry.redwood/issue/embeddings-usw-evict (auto)
Carmen: Here — I'm primary. Quick summary: a burst from a new customer batch job caused unexpected ALL_KEYS scans leading to KV eviction storms in the embeddings caching tier. That caused cascading 503s for the /v1/embeddings path for tenants hitting the hot keys.
Ethan: @Carmen thx. Any customer-impact list yet? I can start outreach if we need SRE/CS help.
Carmen: Initial customer-impact triage: 3 paying tenants saw elevated 5xx; one is high-volume search partner (has retry logic, noticed increased latencies but auto-retries salvaged most requests). No evidence of data loss. Logged as INC-9201.
Carmen: Mitigations applied (chronological):
- increased embeddings cache pool size by +30% (hotfix)
- enabled prefix-KV pinning for the top 5 hot prefixes
- temporarily allowed burst-capacity route to dedicated-reserve pool for critical tenants
- rolled out a fallback model variant (quantized-small) for non-critical tenants to reduce per-request memory
Commands used:
```
# scale primary pool
redwood infra scale --pool embeddings-usw --desired 18
# quick pinning
redwood cache pin --pool embeddings-usw --prefix "tenant:hotkey:" --top 5
```
Carmen: Immediate effect: 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 0.8% over 8 minutes. p95 latency still elevated (~480ms -> 750ms for some requests). No new pages since oncall bot alert.
runbook-bot: Runbook matched: KV-cache-eviction (v2). Recommended steps appended: increase cache pool, pin hot prefixes, enable fallback variant. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction
Priya: Noted. I'll keep an eye on customer retries. I'm standing by to help with postmortem prompt set if needed. Also filing a follow-up to add rate-limits on large-batch ingestion clients (ticket TKT-4556).
Ethan: I'll own post-shift followup and incident blameless doc. For next shift coverage: I can stay late if needed, but I have a calendar conflict 02:00-04:00 UTC (travel). @Leila can you cover that window if we see a regression in EU routes? If not, we should arrange scheduled scaling before I step away.
Leila: I can pick up 02:00-04:00 UTC if required. Ping me in #eng-oncall 15m before. I'll have remote access and can do the pin/unpin ops.
Carmen: Action items for next 24h:
- [ ] Ethan: write incident timeline + initial RCA notes (TKT-9201)
- [ ] Priya: notify affected tenants & coordinate CS messages
- [ ] Leila: standby coverage 02:00-04:00 UTC (EU) if needed
- [ ] Eng-ML: evaluate traffic patterns that triggered ALL_KEYS scan (assign)
- [ ] Infra: add a safety-limit for prefix scan frequency (short-term throttle)
Notes/observations:
- This looks like a client-side design issue (large unbounded ingestion job). We'll propose client-side rate-limit + server-side throttle.
- Pinning hot prefixes prevented the eviction wave; long-term: consider adaptive pinning based on heatmap.
Carmen: Current status: degraded->recovering; user-visible errors reduced to baseline but p95 elevated in small slice of requests. No immediate rollback planned; keep the fallback model in place for 6h while we validate traffic patterns.
Carmen: Handoff for next primary/secondary: primary -> Ethan, secondary -> Priya. Coverage gap: 02:00-04:00 UTC EU (Leila agreed to standby). Please ack.
Ethan: Ack. I'll take primary and start the incident write-up. I'll also schedule a small canary for client throttles tomorrow 0900 PST.
Priya: Acked. I'll coordinate tenant comms and monitor retries.
Leila: Ack. I have the runbook open. If we need to escalate to infra, tag @infra-oncall and ping me.
Carmen: Final: leaving notes in the incident doc and runbook links: https://internal.redwood/incidents/INC-9201 and https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction. Leaving oncall at 23:18 UTC. :wave:
